text:
dana: heads up — our eval CI is flaking on the quantized-llama bring-up. failures only show up with top_p=0.92 + temp=0.7 and only on dedicated-runner, not local single-worker runs.
praveen: huh, is it a seed mismatch or sampling variance?
dana: thought that too, but we pinned rng seed in the harness. repro is inconsistent across CI re-runs (1/5 failures). logs show different token at step 7.
sasha: any stacktrace or token diff?
dana: small excerpt:
```
REQUEST: prompt_id=eval-2026-03-19, seed=1337, top_p=0.92, temp=0.7
OUTPUT A: ... "the treaty"
OUTPUT B: ... "the treay"
```
praveen: typo output indicates nondet decoding, maybe kv cache fetches misaligned when worker resumes? we had a resume path bug awhile back.
maria: also, this only happens with int8 quant kernels enabled, right? Did we try float16 build?
dana: yes — f16 runs are stable. int8 + multi-shard pool triggers it. single-shard int8 also stable. seems to need both quant and shard-resume.
praveen: can you dump RNG state + worker_id at resume boundary? suspect rng stream mixing between workers when we restore sampler state.
dana: added debug dump to runner: `rng_state_hex=...`, `worker=3`, `resume=true` — diffs between runs where failure occurs vs not are subtle: rng state after resume sometimes identical across two workers.
sasha: that would explain same-seed appearance causing interleaved sampling. maybe our seed offset logic uses thread-local RNG but on resume we reattach a global RNG pointer.
praveen: action: dana to add a test that simulates resume with deterministic seeds across 10k sequences and assert no RNG-state collisions. I'll also add a CI job that runs quantized int8+sharded config locally.
dana: created draft patch and local test. patch moves RNG ownership to worker struct and serializes rng_state in checkpoint. also adds guard: assert(rng_owner == worker_id) in resume path.
ci-bot: ci:run pipeline `eval-quant-int8-resume` queued by dana — job id 88231.
maria: if that guard passes, we should also measure perf impact. serialization every resume could add tiny overhead. maybe only to checkpoints or debug builds.
praveen: agreed — make it opt-in behind `--strict-determinism` flag for CI. prod runs keep current fast path.
dana: PR opened: r/eng-ml#483 add rng ownership+strict-determinism flag. linking logs and test vectors in PR.
sasha: nice. also add a short eval harness metric that fails the job if token-level disagreement > 0.1% across reruns — will catch these flappers early. :eyes:
dana: added metric to the test harness. will monitor next CI runs. thanks all. :thumbsup:
